reason: Conversation 1 never raised the spur fuse at all, repeatedly re-asked things the customer had already answered, invented a 'dedicated dishwasher breaker', and ended by telling them to plug a lamp into a fused spur (which has no socket) via a neighbour, which is both impractical and nonsensical. Conversation 2 correctly identified the UK fused-spur setup, explained a safe power-off fuse swap, knew Neff integrated controls sit on the door top, adapted to the customer's inability to pull the unit out, escalated sensibly to an engineer with a useful booking script, and asked for the door-edge model number. Its one weakness is stating a bit too confidently that a lit neon means the spur fuse is fine (the fuse remains a live possibility in the hidden truth), and it listed likely internal parts, though hedged and without telling the customer to buy anything, so it wins clearly rather than decisively.
